initiatives.title: Support sort order in CTAS/RTAS via TBLPROPERTIES
initiatives.summary: Feature request to allow specifying sort order during CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) and REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT (RTAS) operations in Spark SQL, avoiding the need for separate ALTER TABLE commands. The parquet-java implementation ignores the false positive probability (fpp) property when the number of distinct values (ndv) is not specified, making fpp configuration ineffective. The proposal is to add a new table property 'write.parquet.bloom-filter-ndv.column.col1' to the spec and clarify behavior when fpp is specified without ndv.
key_points: Current spec defines bloom-filter-enabled, bloom-filter-max-bytes, and bloom-filter-fpp properties but lacks ndv configuration
Parquet-java ignores fpp values when ndv is not specified, using bloom-filter-max-bytes as exact size instead
Proposal to add write.parquet.bloom-filter-ndv.column.col1 property to enable ndv configuration
Need to clarify spec behavior: should missing ndv with specified fpp be an error, ignored, or use a default value

initiatives.title: FileIO Resource Management Issue in Spark
initiatives.summary: PR #12868 addresses a critical issue where Spark's broadcast variable cleanup calls FileIO.close() and unintentionally shuts down shared resources like HTTP connection pools, breaking Iceberg queries on Spark. The issue is particularly acute with S3FileIO using ApacheHttpClient where all instances share the same connection pool. Community review is requested on the proposed solution and whether a more explicit resource ownership model is needed.
key_points: Spark broadcasts FileIO instances to executors and calls close() during cleanup, terminating shared resources
S3FileIO with ApacheHttpClient is particularly affected as all instances share a single connection pool
The core problem involves broader resource lifecycle management within FileIO
Solution impacts many production Iceberg users on Spark

Index freshness and synchronization with underlying data is a key challenge for global indexing approach

initiatives.title: Cleanup unreferenced statistics files in dropTableData
initiatives.summary: Discussion about orphaned Puffin statistics files remaining in storage after dropTableData() calls. The issue occurs because updateStatistics() creates new metadata versions without deleting old stat files, and dropTableData() only removes files referenced in the latest metadata. The author proposes three alternative solutions with different trade-offs in performance and complexity.
key_points: Old statistics files become orphaned when updateStatistics() is called on existing snapshots
dropTableData() only cleans up stats files in latest metadata, leaving historical ones behind
Three proposed solutions: flag for historical metadata iteration, delete old stats during updates, or track unreferenced files in metadata
Each approach has trade-offs between I/O overhead, complexity, and metadata size
